Ifc33996b492d1d64760f6e31f3966bdb8f230d4.subject: [HP2236BVA-134] Update ONT software version.
Ifc33996b492d1d64760f6e31f3966bdb8f230d4.analysis:
### detailed feedback
<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

- **Potential Command Injection Risk**: The function `update_xpon_sw_version` uses `snprintf` to build a command string and then executes it using `system(cmd)`. While `buffer` is populated via `omci_lib_uci_get`, if that UCI option is ever user-controlled or contains shell metacharacters, it could lead to command injection. 
- **Redundancy**: Use of `system("uci set ...")` is generally less efficient than using UCI library APIs directly if they are available in the same context.
- **Error Handling**: `system()` calls do not check return values.

</details>

I161914405155b2c43e067985e79bf29b76ef35a.subject: [BIFROST-20] HP-2272B|HPM-2272B : implement serial leds and led scenario
I161914405155b2c43e067985e79bf29b76ef35a.analysis:
### detailed feedback
<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

- **Kernel Resource Leak**: In `airoha_sgpio_enable` and `airoha_sgpio_enable_rclk`, `ioremap` is called but `iounmap` is only called in one of them (fixed in this patch), but `ioremap` for `SGPIO_ENABLE_REG_OFFSET` (0x1fa2021c) is done every time the functions are called. It would be better to map this once during `probe` or use a shared mapping.
- **Duplicate labels/nodes**: `an7583_evb_common.dtsi` contains duplicate `thermal_phy: thermal_phy@1efbd000` nodes.
- **Code Quality**: `airoha_sgpio_wait_for_shift` has a busy-wait loop `while (reg_val & BIT(31))` without a timeout or `cpu_relax()`. This could hang the kernel if the hardware doesn't respond as expected.
- **Hardcoded addresses**: Many magic numbers/addresses in `sgpio-airoha.c` (e.g., `0x1fa2021c`) should ideally be in the Device Tree or defined as constants in a header.

</details>

Id720b43fbaca0ff91c89d858f8bb8d6e14238e4.subject: [EUSW-515][APOLLO] Work around DynDNS DDNS TLS stall (WAN egress drop/PMTUD blackhole) by clamping MSS
Id720b43fbaca0ff91c89d858f8bb8d6e14238e4.patch_content:
commit 2cad98a46daf26120f21706557fa2aa179883306
Author: MyeongSooKim <mskim@humax-networks.com>
Date:   Fri Mar 6 12:49:48 2026 +0900

    [EUSW-515][APOLLO] Work around DynDNS DDNS TLS stall (WAN egress drop/PMTUD blackhole) by clamping MSS
    
    - DynDNS(HTTPS/443) updates could stall after the TCP 3-way handshake during TLS ClientHello.
    
    - Under an abnormal server MSS (e.g., 8910) and PMTUD blackhole conditions (no ICMP 'Frag needed'), the large single TLS payload (ClientHello) was observed to not egress from the router WAN interface, i.e., dropped/lost at WAN egress rather than mid-path.
    
    - Clamp MSS on the inadyn socket (TCP_MAXSEG=1460) so ClientHello is segmented under MTU 1500 without relying on PMTUD; confirmed DynDNS update succeeds.
    
    - Changes:
    
    1) Add 004-hmx-forceMss1460.patch: setsockopt(TCP_MAXSEG=1460) before connect() for port 443 and include <netinet/tcp.h>.
    
    2) Update Makefile to apply the new 004 patch during build.
    
    Change-Id: Id720b43fbaca0ff91c89d858f8bb8d6e14238e4e

 		if [ $$? -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi; \
+		patch -p2 -b -s -d$(APP) < patches/004-hmx-forceMss1460.patch; \
+		if [ $$? -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi; \
 	fi;
 endif
 	cd $(APP)

index 00000000000..e15ae9a19df
--- /dev/null
+++ b/userspace/gpl/apps/inadyn/patches/004-hmx-forceMss1460.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+Index: inadyn/inadyn-2.12.0/src/tcp.c
+===================================================================
+--- inadyn.orig/inadyn-2.12.0/src/tcp.c
++++ inadyn/inadyn-2.12.0/src/tcp.c
+@@ -32,6 +32,7 @@
+ #include <arpa/nameser.h>
+ #include <net/if.h>
+ #include <netinet/in.h>
++#include <netinet/tcp.h>
+ #include <resolv.h>
+ 
+ #include "http.h"
+@@ -179,6 +180,14 @@ int tcp_init(tcp_sock_t *tcp, char *msg,
+ 			if (getnameinfo(sa, len, host, sizeof(host), NULL, 0, NI_NUMERICHOST))
+ 				goto next;
+ 
++			/* [EUSW-515] Force conservative MSS for HTTPS(443) to avoid PMTUD blackhole */
++			if (tcp->port == 443) {
++				int mss = 1460;
++				if (setsockopt(sd, IPPROTO_TCP, TCP_MAXSEG, &mss, sizeof(mss)) < 0) {
++					logit(LOG_INFO, "Failed setting TCP_MAXSEG=%d: %s", mss, strerror(errno));
++				}
++			}
++
+ 			set_timeouts(sd, tcp->timeout);
+ 
+ 			logit(LOG_INFO, "%s, %sconnecting to %s([%s]:%d)", msg, tries ? "re" : "",
